samples.summary: Dropping `label: true` from markdown-it-task-lists is an unrequested rendering change that removes the accessible name from every task checkbox (read-only previews included). The issue only asked for clickable task items; the `<label>`-forwards-the-click problem could have been solved by ignoring clicks whose target is a label-forwarded synthetic event, or by keeping the label and skipping the duplicate. As shipped, screen-reader users get an unlabeled checkbox and the label/text association that existed before this PR is gone.
samples.evidence: was `md.use(taskLists, { label: true, enabled: false })`; now `md.use(taskLists, { enabled: true })` with a comment saying the label wrapper is deliberately off

samples.summary: Line-block prefix rewriting is now implemented twice in the same package: `toggleQuote` in commands.ts already iterates the selected lines, builds one ChangeSet and maps the selection with assoc 1 (the new `replacePrefixes` comment even says "as `toggleQuote` does"). The shared helper was not extracted, so the two block-level markdown commands drift independently.

`computeActiveFormats` now parses every line the selection covers (`selectedTargets` → regex per line) on every selection/doc change, where it previously only sliced a few chars around the caret. A select-all in a long note therefore runs one regex per document line on each keystroke; the toolbar only needs the shared kind plus two booleans, which could be computed from the first/last line or bounded.
samples.evidence: computeActiveFormats calls computeListState(state) unconditionally; computeListState → selectedTargets iterates all selected lines

samples.summary: Interaction policy that arguably belongs to the host app (double-click = word select, drag-select suppression, `details`/link/button exemptions, nested-`li` disambiguation) is baked into the engine's preview class with no way for a host to override it. Reasonable for now, but it makes `NotePreview` the owner of click semantics rather than exposing the hit-test and letting the editor decide.
samples.evidence: onTaskClick contains five distinct bail-out heuristics
